agent.name: Silver-Milk Team Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Dated technology-landscape intelligence: eight fixed landscape dimensions (capability, use cases, trackers, ecosystem, standards, price/performance, coverage, alternatives) each with a basis, broad signals separated from the few that matter to this organization, execution gates kept apart from landscape signals, a gating-condition x movement table that sets the monitoring stance, owned triggers mapped to actions, and a dated stale/hype flag (never the adoption decision, never a vendor selection)

analytical_question: Where does this emerging technology and application sit in the current landscape of alternatives, complements, ecosystems, standards, regulation, investment and adoption signals, and what should this organization monitor next?
general_et_finding:
AS OF: 2026-11-17
UNIT: Text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the historical reference architecture.
L1 TECHNICAL CAPABILITY: Developing — Human ratings for the diffusion-family FLUX.1 Krea dev show useful text-guided results with material variation in prompt fidelity; the benchmark does not establish routine reliability (ImagenWorld, 2026-04). BASIS: E1
L2 USE-CASE EVIDENCE: Use cases emerging — A named campaign used DALL·E 2, whose decoder was diffusion-based; one campaign does not establish recurring use (The Drum, 2022-07; OpenAI, 2022-04). BASIS: E2, E3
L3 TRACKER PLACEMENT: Not covered by Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 35, 2026-11-04 — No category placement in the edition (Thoughtworks, 2026-11). BASIS: E4
L4 VENDOR/ECOSYSTEM STRUCTURE: Consolidating — Creative suites bundle outside models while providers still offer API and downloadable routes; market shares are unverified (Adobe, 2026-11; Black Forest Labs, 2026-01). BASIS: E5, E6
L5 STANDARDS & REGULATION: Emerging — U.S. Copyright Office guidance applies existing authorship principles across generative AI; the report is agency interpretation rather than a diffusion-specific rule (U.S. Copyright Office, 2025-01). BASIS: E7
L6 PRICE/PERFORMANCE: Mixed — Posted FLUX tiers vary by model, resolution and reference inputs; available rates and vendor speed claims do not establish a 12-month trend at constant output quality (Black Forest Labs, 2026-01; pricing opened 2026-11). BASIS: E5, E8
L7 COVERAGE TONE: Mixed — Speed and access coverage alongside reporting on contested training-data rights (VentureBeat, 2026-01; Bloomberg Law, 2026-07). BASIS: E9, E10
L8 ALTERNATIVES & COMPLEMENTS: INCUMBENT: Manual designer-led image composition. COMPETING: Native autoregressive image generation and reference-based editing. COMPLEMENTS: Reference libraries, conventional editors, asset management and human review.
POSITION: Diffusion can generate useful images on bounded tasks, and named commercial use exists. Repeatable production evidence and comparable workflow economics remain uneven.
application_finding:
APPLICATION SIGNALS: L1 determines whether drafts follow the brief and preserve recognizable reference details during iteration. L2 distinguishes a working concept-board process from a showcase. L6 matters because retries, review and manual corrections determine the cost of a usable board.
APPLICATION-SPECIFIC EVIDENCE: Thin — Independent human evaluation covers related generation and reference tasks, but no retrieved independent field comparison measures disposable internal homeware-advertising boards against designer-led work.
STRONGEST ALTERNATIVE: Manual designer-led image composition — It can reuse exact product-photo pixels while varying layout, color and surrounding imagery.
organization_specific_finding:
UNIT OF ANALYSIS: The hypothetical U.S. homeware retailer’s creative operations and procurement decision about preparing a bounded comparison.
GATING CONDITION: The fast-follower retailer needs documented reference-capable options and credible external evidence that catalog-based boards can preserve product details at a competitive all-in workflow cost.
CONDITION STATUS: Partly met — Options are documented and related tasks have been evaluated, but matched evidence on fidelity and workflow cost is missing. BASIS: E1, E5, E6, E8
MOVEMENT: None — Recent sources document options, benchmarks and metering without showing a comparable improvement in catalog-faithful board cost. BASIS: E1, E5, E6, E8
STANCE: Scheduled watch
EXECUTION GATES: Exact product and plan terms, privacy and retention, security clearance and procurement review — security/procurement review function; rights to upload catalog inputs and use outputs — owner not stated; trial authorization — owner not stated.
RELEVANT SIGNALS: L1 shows variable prompt and reference fidelity, making catalog-photo checks consequential. L4 shows integrated and downloadable routes, so the creative operations lead can compare integration burden and portability. L6 shows per-generation and reference-input metering, which matters because the approved software budget does not establish cost per usable board.
POPULAR BUT NOT DECISIVE HERE: Subsecond generation headlines measure model latency; they say little about the time marketers spend correcting a product detail.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DEVELOPMENT: L1 — Independent human-rated diagnostics expose where image edits fail, making reference preservation the first question when deciding whether to prepare a bounded comparison.
ECOSYSTEM DEPENDENCY: The chosen model runtime’s interface for reference inputs and versioned outputs.
OPTIONS DOCUMENTED: FLUX.2 [klein] 4B — vendor-claim, downloadable weights and hosted metering for text generation and reference editing; Adobe Firefly Boards with partner models — vendor-claim, integrated access to partner image models; OpenAI 4o native image generation — vendor-claim, autoregressive reference-based generation and editing documented at launch, with current access unverified. NO SELECTION.

evidence.claim: E1: ImagenWorld reports model-level human evaluations on open-ended image tasks. FLUX.1 Krea dev shows useful but variable prompt adherence in text-guided generation. Separate editing results help identify reference and local-edit failure modes.
evidence.source_or_reference: ImagenWorld, ICLR 2026, Table 1 and evaluation discussion. https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/458fa8ee331566383d8e74bdb647f829-Paper-Conference.pdf
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: independent; LOAD-BEARING. L1 uses the named diffusion-family model result, not the pooled result across architectures. The study is a task benchmark rather than a commercial deployment or retailer cost comparison.

evidence.claim: E2: Heinz and Rethink used DALL·E 2 imagery for the public A.I. Ketchup campaign.
evidence.source_or_reference: The Drum, campaign coverage, and the campaign’s Applied Arts entry. https://www.thedrum.com/news/ad-the-day-what-happens-when-heinz-asks-ai-image-generator-draw-ketchup | https://www.appliedartsmag.com/winners/a-i-ketchup-w495?year=2022
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: industry-analyst; UNDERLYING: Heinz and Rethink’s A.I. Ketchup campaign; LOAD-BEARING. The award entry and trade coverage describe one campaign and count as one production claim.

evidence.claim: E3: OpenAI documents a diffusion decoder in the DALL·E 2 architecture used to identify the technology in E2.
evidence.source_or_reference: OpenAI, Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents. https://openai.com/index/hierarchical-text-conditional-image-generation-with-clip-latents/
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: vendor-claim; LOAD-BEARING. Architectural classification only.

evidence.claim: E4: Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 35 publishes ring placements for selected technologies but does not place text-to-image diffusion models as a category.
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: industry-analyst; LOAD-BEARING. Category omission gives no movement or market-wide adoption measure.

evidence.claim: E5: Black Forest Labs released FLUX.2 [klein] variants for text-to-image and reference-based editing, with downloadable weights and vendor-reported latency measurements on an NVIDIA GB200.
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: vendor-claim; LOAD-BEARING. Availability and the reported test setup are documented; workflow speed and fidelity are unverified.

evidence.claim: E6: Adobe lists Adobe and partner image workflows across Creative Cloud, including access to partner models from Firefly Boards.
evidence.source_or_reference: Adobe Help, Partner models in Adobe products. https://helpx.adobe.com/creative-cloud/apps/generative-ai/non-adobe-models-in-adobe-products.html
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: vendor-claim; LOAD-BEARING. Distribution and integration documentation; specific plan entitlements and data terms remain unverified.

evidence.claim: E7: The U.S. Copyright Office’s generative AI output report explains how existing human-authorship principles apply to copyrightability.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability. https://www.copyright.gov/newsnet/2025/1060.html
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: standards-regulatory; LOAD-BEARING. Agency interpretation of existing law. The report does not grant catalog-input rights or decide the copyright status of a specific board.

evidence.claim: E8: Black Forest Labs lists different resolution and reference-input charges across hosted image models, including FLUX.2 [klein] 4B per-megapixel metering.
evidence.source_or_reference: Black Forest Labs, pricing calculator and model rate tables. https://bfl.ai/pricing
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: vendor-claim; LOAD-BEARING. Posted rates establish available billing structures. A matched historical series and labor costs are missing.

evidence.claim: E9: VentureBeat’s FLUX.2 [klein] coverage emphasized speed and access to downloadable models.
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: industry-analyst; UNDERLYING: Black Forest Labs FLUX.2 [klein] release for the latency claim; LOAD-BEARING for coverage tone only. The release and coverage do not independently corroborate performance.

evidence.claim: E10: Bloomberg Law covered a complaint alleging unlicensed use of automotive photographs in Midjourney training.
evidence.source_or_reference: Bloomberg Law, Midjourney Copied Thousands of Car Photos to Train AI, Suit Says. https://news.bloomberglaw.com/litigation/midjourney-copied-thousands-of-car-photos-to-train-ai-suit-says
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: industry-analyst; UNDERLYING: EVOX Productions complaint; LOAD-BEARING for coverage tone only. The complaint contains allegations.

evidence.claim: E11: OpenAI’s 4o native image generation system card describes an autoregressive image model with image transformation capabilities.
evidence.source_or_reference: OpenAI, Addendum to GPT-4o System Card: Native Image Generation. https://cdn.openai.com/11998be9-5319-4302-bfbf-1167e093f1fb/Native_Image_Generation_System_Card.pdf
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run; SOURCE CLASS: vendor-claim. Architectural comparator and historical feature documentation. Current access was not verified.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: COMPETING READING: Background scan — If the external gate requires a comparable deployment with measured labor and reference-fidelity results before comparison planning carries any value, the benchmark and product documentation leave that stricter gate unmet.
CHASM EVIDENCE FOR: E2 (2022-07) records diffusion-generated images used in a public Heinz campaign, with the model architecture verified by E3.

CHASM EVIDENCE AGAINST: E1 (2026-04) reports variable human-rated prompt adherence for a named diffusion-family model on open-ended generation tasks. That is evidence of continued review needs; it does not measure deployment prevalence.

DISTINGUISHING EVIDENCE: A dated independent field report tracing recurring catalog-based concept-board work across retailers and disclosing model version, product-fidelity rejections, review labor, integration effort and the manual baseline.

STALE/HYPE FLAG: E5 (2026-01-15), Black Forest Labs’ subsecond generation claim for FLUX.2 [klein] — measured on a GB200 and sensitive to deployment, model version and inputs. CONTROL: Used to describe the vendor's documented test and coverage; movement and workflow cost require comparable task evidence. REFRESH BY: 2026-12-18.
The second organization’s full case and result were not supplied. Its gating condition and stance could not be verified against this contrast.
L6 Mixed reflects documented tier and metering variation with limited comparability. A category-wide 12-month direction at fixed accepted-output quality remains unverified.
confidence_and_uncertainty: CONFIDENCE: Moderate — Broad landscape confidence is moderate for bounded generation capability, documented deployment options and the inspected tracker, and lower for recurring production prevalence and constant-quality price direction. Confidence in local relevance is moderate for catalog fidelity and portability, and low for net workflow savings. A category placement from Gartner, IEEE, Forrester or IDC and an independent matched retailer field study were not retrieved.
value_opportunity_implication: The retailer’s photo repository, established review process and named creative operations lead make it possible to compare time and cost per accepted internal board. Count integration effort, retries, manual touch-ups, review and metered image charges against the same designer-led brief.
risk_governance_implication: Prioritize catalog-image rights and privacy at the execution gate, then rank options by reference fidelity, portability and all-in workflow cost. Keep generated concepts in the internal board workflow and preserve the existing independent checks on final product photography.
recommendation_management_implication: STANCE: Scheduled watch — WATCH FIRST: An independent matched-task comparison of reference fidelity and cost per usable board, including review and rework. Compare catalog integration and export portability once a plausible workflow advantage is documented. STRONGEST ALTERNATIVE: Manual designer-led image composition. REFRESH: Quarterly, with a full source refresh at least annually and a management checkpoint within the six-week review.
change_monitoring_triggers: TRIGGER 1 [L1] CAPABILITY: A dated independent comparative evaluation reports materially fewer product-attribute errors in catalog-reference edits at a matched review effort — threshold pending creative operations lead approval — SOURCE: peer-reviewed benchmark or independent lab report — OWNER: creative operations lead (proposed) — CADENCE: quarterly → Active watch, inspect the evaluation method and hand off local test planning.

TRIGGER 2 [L2] USE-CASE: A dated independent retailer field report documents recurring product-faithful concept boards at lower all-in cost per accepted board than a matched manual workflow — threshold pending creative operations lead approval — SOURCE: independent retail workflow study — OWNER: creative operations lead (proposed) — CADENCE: quarterly → Landscape not the constraint, after verifying applicability to the stated gate.

TRIGGER 3 [L6] REVERSAL: A dated independent cross-provider comparison finds that available reference-capable workflows consistently cost more per accepted concept board than manual composition at matched fidelity — threshold pending creative operations lead approval — SOURCE: independent workflow cost study — OWNER: creative operations lead (proposed) — CADENCE: quarterly → Background scan.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: MORE INFO → Matched manual baseline, required product attributes and export needs: These determine whether external fidelity, portability and workflow-cost findings transfer to the retailer.
MORE INFO → Exact product, plan and gate owners: These identify whose terms apply and who can clear catalog input rights, retention, security and trial authorization.
HANDOFF → Creation Agent: How did latent diffusion and subsequent conditioning methods emerge?
HANDOFF → Innovation Agent: How should the lifecycle and DEGREE of the specific workflow innovation be classified?
HANDOFF → Promethean Agent: How significant is the change in how creative labor is allocated?
HANDOFF → Diffusion Agent: What stage and timing are supported for repeat use of diffusion in comparable creative workflows?
HANDOFF → Adoption Agent: What management action follows, and what design would support a valid comparison if separately authorized?
HANDOFF → Organizational Adoption Agent: Can the retailer run and govern the workflow, and who clears each execution gate?
